column1: A point charge in a vacuum is accelerated by the Coulomb force exerted by another fixed point charge. A charged small ball slides on a horizontal rail, affected by the Coulomb force of another fixed charged small ball. A charged block slides down a slope, influenced by the Coulomb repulsion from a fixed point charge at the top of the slope. Two charged small balls with like charges repel and separate on a frictionless horizontal plane. A charged small ball and a charged cube attract each other and collide on a smooth surface. A charged small ball at the center of a square frame is influenced by the Coulomb forces of fixed point charges at the four corners. A charged small ball accelerates downward in an electric field perpendicular to the ground. A charged cube placed on a charged plane experiences an upward Coulomb repulsion. Two charged small balls connected by an insulating rod rotate around their center of mass on a horizontal plane. A charged small ball moves in a circular orbit, attracted by a central fixed point charge. A charged small ball placed directly above a charged disk with uniform charge density is attracted. A charged ball moves with constant velocity in an electric field perpendicular to a charged plate. Two charged points at the ends of an insulating line repel each other, straightening the line. A charged small ball at the center of a charged ring remains stationary due to the net force of the ring's charges. A charged ball in an electric field is repelled by a cube with like charges and begins to accelerate. A charged small ball slides along the outer surface of a charged cylinder under the influence of the Coulomb force.
